title: EPA Finalizes 2020 Changes to Coal Ash Closure Rules
description_short: On July 29, 2020, EPA finalized coal ash closure revisions, including retrofit or closure requirements for unlined impoundments and broader public access to data.
description_medium: On July 29, 2020, EPA finalized revisions to federal coal ash regulations. The rule required all unlined surface impoundments, including compacted-soil-lined units reclassified as unlined, to retrofit or close. It set April 11, 2021, for affected units to stop receiving waste and begin closure or retrofit, and revised public reporting requirements while retaining the major protections of the 2015 rule.
description_long: On July 29, 2020, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalized revisions to federal regulations for coal combustion residuals (CCR), commonly called coal ash, from electric utilities. In response to court rulings, the rule required all unlined surface impoundments to retrofit or close, including units that had not detected groundwater contamination above regulatory levels. It reclassified compacted-soil-lined, or “clay-lined,” surface impoundments as unlined, bringing those units within the retrofit-or-close requirement. EPA set April 11, 2021, as the date by which unlined impoundments and units that failed the aquifer location restriction had to stop receiving waste and initiate closure or retrofit. The rule also revised annual groundwater monitoring and corrective-action reports, including an executive-summary requirement, and changed coal-ash website rules so required facility information would be immediately available to the public. EPA also gave certain facilities more time to develop alternative capacity for waste streams before stopping waste receipt and beginning closure. The agency said the 2015 inspection, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting requirements remained in place, with two public-access enhancements.

facts.quote: Today, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalized several changes to the regulations for coal combustion residuals, known as CCR or coal ash, to implement the court’s vacatur of certain closure requirements as well as adding provisions that enhance the public’s access to information about the management of coal ash at electric utilities.
all unlined surface impoundments are required to retrofit or close, not just those that have detected groundwater contamination above regulatory levels.

The rule also changes the classification of compacted-soil lined or “clay-lined” surface impoundments from “lined” to “unlined,” which means that formerly defined clay-lined surface impoundments are no longer considered lined surface impoundments and need to be retrofitted or closed.

the rule establishes a revised date, April 11, 2021, by which unlined surface impoundments and units that failed the aquifer location restriction must cease receiving waste and initiate closure or retrofit.
The 2015 requirements for facility inspection, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting requirements are also unchanged except for two enhancements to public access to information.

Revising the annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report requirements to make the data easier for the public to understand and evaluate, including a requirement to summarize the results in an executive summary.
Revising the CCR website requirements to ensure that relevant facility information required by the regulations is immediately available to the public.
EPA is also finalizing revisions to the alternative closure provisions that would grant certain facilities additional time to develop alternative capacity to manage their waste streams
